problem: What is ${\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?

activity_context.topic_title: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums

feedback.problem:
Express ${\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+2x+1)\,\text{d}x$ as the limit of a left Riemann sum.

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+2x+1)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[(($
{{field-1}}
$)^{3}+2($
{{field-2}}
$)+1)\cdot \frac{2}{n}]$
feedback.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+2x+1)\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)={x}^{3}+2x+1,$ the lower bound is $a=0,$ and the upper bound is $b=2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{2-0}{n}=\frac{2}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{3}+2x+1)\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(0+i\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(\frac{2i}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[({(\,\frac{2i}{n}\,)}^{3}+2(\,\frac{2i}{n}\,)+1)\,\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
